byTheNumbers.title: The year in numbers
byTheNumbers.standfirst: Latest official figures, each shown with the period it covers.

items.title: Unemployment rate
items.summary: The unemployment rate was 4.2 percent in September 2026.

sources.label: BLS: The Employment Situation, September 2026 (2 October 2026)
BLS via FRED: Unemployment rate (UNRATE)

items.title: Average hourly earnings
items.summary: Private-sector employees earned an average of $37.81 an hour in September 2026, up 3.0 percent over 12 months.

sources.label: BLS: The Employment Situation, September 2026 (2 October 2026)
BLS via FRED: Average hourly earnings of all employees, total private (CES0500000003)

items.metric: Average hourly earnings, all private employees

items.title: Mortgage rate
items.summary: The 30-year fixed mortgage rate averaged 7.40 percent in the week to 15 October 2026, against 6.27 percent a year earlier.

sources.label: FRED: 30-year fixed rate mortgage average in the United States (Freddie Mac)
Freddie Mac: Primary Mortgage Market Survey (week of 15 October 2026)

items.title: Consumer prices
items.summary: Prices were 3.7 percent higher in September 2026 than a year earlier; without food and energy the rise was 2.6 percent, and energy alone was up 20.4 percent.

sources.label: BLS: Consumer Price Index, September 2026 (14 October 2026)

items.title: A typical weekly pay packet
items.summary: Full-time wage and salary workers had median usual weekly earnings of $1,251 in the second quarter of 2026, 4.6 percent more than a year before.

sources.label: BLS: Usual weekly earnings of wage and salary workers, second quarter 2026 (21 July 2026)

items.metric: Median usual weekly earnings, full-time workers

items.title: Hiring slowed
items.summary: Employers added 29,000 jobs in September 2026 and the workweek averaged 34.4 hours.

sources.label: BLS: The Employment Situation, September 2026 (2 October 2026)

items.title: Eggs a third cheaper
items.summary: A dozen eggs cost $2.27 in September 2026, against $3.49 a year earlier.

BLS via FRED: Utility (piped) gas per therm (APU000072620)

items.title: Eating in versus eating out
items.summary: Food bought for the home cost 1.8 percent more than a year earlier in September 2026, while restaurant and takeaway food cost 3.5 percent more.

sources.label: BLS: Consumer Price Index, September 2026 (14 October 2026)

clothingAndStyle.title: What people wore
clothingAndStyle.standfirst: Clothes cost a little more, and secondhand kept growing.

items.title: Clothes cost more
items.summary: Clothing prices were 3.4 percent higher in September 2026 than a year earlier.

sources.label: BLS: Consumer Price Index, September 2026 (14 October 2026)

items.title: Secondhand takes off
items.summary: ThredUp's 2026 Resale Report said the U.S. secondhand clothing market grew nearly four times faster than the broader clothing market in 2025.

sources.label: Retail Dive: US resale market to surpass $78B by 2030 (3 April 2026, on ThredUp's 2026 Resale Report)

items.title: Secondhand by 2030
items.summary: ThredUp (with GlobalData) forecast that U.S. secondhand clothing sales would reach about $78.8 billion by 2030, growing about 7.3 percent a year.

sources.label: Retail Dive: US resale market to surpass $78B by 2030 (3 April 2026, on ThredUp's 2026 Resale Report)

items.title: Back-to-school shopping
items.summary: The National Retail Federation estimated that families with school-age children would spend about $864 each on back-to-school items in 2026, including about $174 on shoes.

sources.label: Finder, citing NRF: Back-to-school spending (as reported in search results)

clothingAndStyle.scarcityNote: Year in progress, and the fashion trade publishes few official 2026 figures. Four items are shown; the NRF and ThredUp pages could not be opened directly.

workAndWages.title: Work and wages
workAndWages.standfirst: Hiring slowed, pay rose about 3 percent, and layoffs hit tech and media.

items.title: Median full-time pay
items.summary: Median usual weekly earnings of full-time workers were $1,251 in the second quarter of 2026.

sources.label: BLS: Usual weekly earnings of wage and salary workers, second quarter 2026 (21 July 2026)

items.job: All full-time wage and salary workers (median)

items.title: Women's and men's pay
items.summary: Women's median weekly earnings were $1,131 and men's $1,380 in the second quarter of 2026, so women earned 82.0 percent of what men did.

sources.label: BLS: Usual weekly earnings of wage and salary workers, second quarter 2026 (21 July 2026)

items.title: Who works from home
items.summary: In June 2026, 52.5 percent of workers in financial activities teleworked, against 47.2 percent in information and 7.7 percent in leisure and hospitality.

sources.label: BLS TED: 52.5 percent of workers in financial activities teleworked in June 2026 (29 July 2026)

items.title: Layoffs in tech and media
items.summary: Epic Games announced more than 1,000 layoffs on 24 March, Microsoft said on 6 July it would cut 1,600 Xbox jobs now and 1,600 more over the next year, and Netflix said in October it would cut about 1,000 jobs.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 2026 in video games
Wikipedia: Netflix

items.title: A slow September
items.summary: Employers added 29,000 jobs in September 2026 and the unemployment rate stayed at 4.2 percent.

sources.label: BLS: The Employment Situation, September 2026 (2 October 2026)
BLS via FRED: Unemployment rate (UNRATE)

schoolAndChildhood.title: Growing up
schoolAndChildhood.standfirst: Teens leaned on chatbots for schoolwork, and phones were locked away in more schools.

items.title: Chatbots for schoolwork
items.summary: Pew found that 54 percent of U.S. teens had used a chatbot for help with schoolwork, and 10 percent did all or most of their schoolwork with its help.

sources.label: Pew Research Center: How teens use and view AI (24 February 2026)

items.metric: Teens who have used chatbots for schoolwork

items.title: Is it cheating?
items.summary: About 59 percent of teens said AI cheating happens at least somewhat often at their school.

sources.label: Pew Research Center: How teens use and view AI (24 February 2026)

items.metric: Teens who say AI cheating happens at least somewhat often

items.title: Phones away
items.summary: Several states restrict phones in class; in Oregon, where districts had to enforce a ban by 2026, 99 percent had done so by February 2026.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Mobile phone use in schools

items.title: The back-to-school bill
items.summary: The NRF estimated families with school-age children would spend about $864 each in 2026, a record total of about $43 billion.

sources.label: Finder, citing NRF: Back-to-school spending (as reported in search results)

items.title: How many pupils
items.summary: U.S. public schools enrolled about 48.8 million students in fall 2024, 0.3 percent fewer than in fall 2023; a fall 2025 national count was not yet available.

sources.label: Florida Education Association: 2026 Rankings and Estimates Report (April 2026)

gettingAround.title: Getting around
gettingAround.standfirst: Flying set a summer record while pump prices jumped.

items.title: A busy day at the airport
items.summary: TSA screened 2,988,204 people on 18 June 2026, the highest single day in its 2026 table.

sources.label: TSA: TSA checkpoint travel numbers (2026)

items.metric: People screened at U.S. airport checkpoints in one day

items.title: Pump prices jump
items.summary: Gasoline prices were 34.2 percent higher in September 2026 than a year earlier, and energy as a whole was up 20.4 percent.

sources.label: BLS: Consumer Price Index, September 2026 (14 October 2026)

items.title: Driverless rides to the airport
items.summary: Waymo opened San Francisco International Airport to a waitlist on 29 January 2026 and Nashville International on 13 October.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Waymo

sources.label: Wikipedia: 2026 in the United States

items.summary: Long Island Rail Road workers went on strike on 16 May 2026.

keepingInTouch.title: Keeping in touch
keepingInTouch.standfirst: Phones got more expensive to fold, and scams found people by text.

items.title: A folding iPhone
items.summary: Apple said its first folding iPhone, the iPhone Duo, goes on sale on 23 October 2026 from $1,999, with pre-orders from 16 October.

sources.label: Apple Newsroom: Apple unveils iPhone Duo (9 September 2026)

items.title: Scams cost billions
items.summary: The FTC told Congress that consumers reported $15.9 billion in fraud losses in 2025 from about 3 million reports; investment scams cost the most, $7.9 billion.

sources.label: FTC: FTC testifies before the Joint Economic Committee on its efforts to combat fraud (25 March 2026)

items.metric: Fraud losses reported to the FTC

items.summary: A Verizon outage on 14 January 2026 affected at least 175,000 people.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 2026 in the United States

items.title: Dish in the sky
items.summary: Starlink reported more than 12 million customers by June 2026, up from about 10.3 million in March.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Starlink

healthAndMedicine.title: Health and medicine
healthAndMedicine.standfirst: Weight-loss drugs went mainstream, and measles returned in force.

items.title: Weight-loss drugs
items.summary: Gallup found that 11 percent of U.S. adults were taking a GLP-1 drug for weight loss in 2026, up from 3 percent in 2024.

sources.label: Gallup: In U.S., GLP-1 usage reaches new high (7 July 2026, updated 8 September 2026)

items.metric: Adults currently taking a GLP-1 drug for weight loss

items.title: Obesity rate
items.summary: Gallup's self-reported obesity rate fell to 36.8 percent in 2026 from a peak of 39.9 percent in 2022.

sources.label: Gallup: In U.S., GLP-1 usage reaches new high (7 July 2026, updated 8 September 2026)

items.title: Measles returns
items.summary: The CDC counted 4,410 confirmed measles cases in 2026 by 15 October, against 2,289 in all of 2025; about 96 percent were linked to outbreaks.

sources.label: CDC: Measles cases and outbreaks (as of 15 October 2026)

sensitivity.note: This item touches on an outbreak of infectious disease.

items.title: Leaving the WHO
items.summary: The United States left the World Health Organization on 22 January 2026.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 2026 in the United States

healthAndMedicine.scarcityNote: Year in progress. Four items are shown; no recent national figure for life expectancy or insurance cover could be opened.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 2026 Winter Olympics

items.summary: Spider-Man: Brand New Day had a record U.S. and Canada opening weekend of $360 million and had earned about $2.5 billion worldwide by mid-October.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 2026 in film

spotlight.title: Living with AI assistants
spotlight.standfirst: Living with AI assistants: how ordinary people used chatbots in 2026.

items.title: Half of adults
items.summary: About half of U.S. adults, 49 percent, said in February 2026 that they use AI chatbots, up from about a third in 2024.

sources.label: Pew Research Center: About half of U.S. adults now use AI chatbots, up from a third in 2024 (11 June 2026)

items.title: Teens and daily use
items.summary: Pew reported that about three in ten teens use chatbots daily.

sources.label: Pew Research Center: How teens use and view AI (24 February 2026)

items.title: What parents know
items.summary: About half of parents said their teen uses chatbots, while 64 percent of teens said they do.

sources.label: Pew Research Center: How teens use and view AI (24 February 2026)

items.title: What teens ask
items.summary: Among teens, 57 percent had used chatbots to search for information, 47 percent for fun, 16 percent for casual conversation and 12 percent for emotional support or advice.

sources.label: Pew Research Center: How teens use and view AI (24 February 2026)

items.summary: Florida's attorney general sued OpenAI over ChatGPT on 1 June 2026, the first such suit by a state.
